intro: Business signage does more work than almost anything else you'll buy for your premises. It tells people you're there, shows them the way in, and sets the tone before anyone has spoken to you. We design and make business signs for shops, offices, pubs, cafés, schools, sites and car parks, from a single door sign to a full set for a new building.

Start with the type of sign you need. [Acrylic signs](/business-signs/acrylic-signs/) and [3D letters](/business-signs/3d-letters/) give receptions and offices a polished finish. [Dibond aluminium signs](/business-signs/dibond-aluminium-signs/) and [outdoor signs](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/) are built to stand up to Norfolk weather. [Illuminated signs](/business-signs/illuminated-signs/) keep you visible after dark, and [pavement signs](/business-signs/pavement-signs/) pull passing trade through the door.

Every sign is made to order. Choose the size, material and fixings on the product page, send us your logo or wording, and we'll send a proof to approve before anything goes into production. If you don't have artwork, our design studio can set it up for you or create something new.

Not sure what will work? Tell us where the sign is going, how far away people will read it from and whether it's inside or out, and we'll recommend the right product. We can also fit signs for businesses across Norfolk and Suffolk.

faqs.q: What file do I need to send for my logo?
faqs.a: A vector file (AI, EPS, SVG or a PDF made from design software) gives the sharpest result. If you only have a JPG or PNG, send it anyway and we'll tell you whether it's good enough or offer to redraw it.

faqs.q: Can you design the sign for me?
faqs.a: Yes. Our studio can lay out your wording and logo, or design a new sign from scratch. You'll see a proof before anything is made.

faqs.q: Do you fit signs?
faqs.a: We fit signs for businesses across Norfolk and Suffolk. Further afield, we supply signs with the fixings you've chosen and clear instructions.

faqs.q: Which material is best for outdoor signs?
faqs.a: Aluminium composite (Dibond) is the most popular choice for long-term outdoor signs. Acrylic, foamex and correx all work outdoors too, with different lifespans and budgets. Our [Foamex vs aluminium composite vs correx guide](/signage-home/compare/foamex-vs-aluminium-composite-vs-correx/) compares them.

intro: Acrylic signs are the go-to choice for offices, receptions, salons and clinics that want a clean, modern look. The material is rigid, glossy and crisp at the edges, and it takes print beautifully, so your logo looks sharp and colours stay bright.

Most of our acrylic signs are printed on the back of a clear or coloured panel. Viewed from the front, the print sits behind a protective layer of acrylic, which gives it depth and keeps it safe from scratches and cleaning. A white ink layer behind the colours stops them looking washed out on clear material.

Choose from clear, frosted, black, white, glass-effect, recycled and glitter acrylic. Panels come as rectangles or can be cut to the outline of your logo, and you can pick from 3mm, 5mm and 10mm thicknesses on many signs. Thicker acrylic looks more substantial on a wall, especially when mounted on stand-offs.

Fixing options include polished stand-offs, which hold the sign away from the wall for a floating effect, as well as hidden fixings and adhesive pads for walls you'd rather not drill. Acrylic is suitable for indoor use and many signs work outside too; check each product for details.

Acrylic is often called Perspex, a well-known brand of the same material. Comparing options? See our [built-up letters vs flat panel signs guide](/signage-home/compare/built-up-letters-vs-flat-panel-signs/) or browse [3D letters](/business-signs/3d-letters/).

faqs.q: Is acrylic the same as Perspex?
faqs.a: Yes. Perspex is a brand name for acrylic sheet, and the terms are used interchangeably. Our acrylic signs are made from cast acrylic sheet.

faqs.q: Can acrylic signs go outside?
faqs.a: Many can. Reverse-printed acrylic is well protected, and our outdoor clear acrylic sign is made for external walls. Very large panels in exposed spots may suit aluminium composite better.

faqs.q: What thickness should I choose?
faqs.a: 5mm suits most office and door signs. 10mm gives a heavier, more premium look on reception walls and is the best match for stand-offs on larger signs. 3mm is lighter and more economical for small signs.

faqs.q: How are acrylic signs fixed to the wall?
faqs.a: Usually with stand-offs (metal spacers that screw to the wall), with hidden rear fixings, or with strong adhesive tape on smooth surfaces. You can choose on each product page.

intro: Dibond signs are the workhorse of outdoor business signage. Dibond is a brand of aluminium composite panel: two thin skins of aluminium bonded to a solid core. It's rigid, flat, light enough to fix easily, and it won't rot, rust or warp in the weather.

We print directly onto the panel in full colour, so you can have photos, gradients and brand colours rather than just simple lettering. For exposed sites we add a protective laminate, including an anti-graffiti finish that lets paint and marker pen be cleaned off without damaging the print.

Choose from white, black, brushed silver and brushed brass-effect panels. Signs can be rectangular, cut to the outline of your logo, or folded into a tray sign with returned edges for shop fascias and building fronts.

Aluminium signs suit building exteriors, car parks, gates, schools, industrial units and anywhere a sign needs to last for years outdoors. Indoors, brushed finishes look smart in offices and receptions. Fix them flat with screw caps, float them on stand-offs, or mount them on [posts](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/).

Weighing up materials? Our [foamex vs aluminium composite vs correx comparison](/signage-home/compare/foamex-vs-aluminium-composite-vs-correx/) explains the differences, and we also make [aluminium composite panels](/signage-home/large-format-print/aluminium-composite-panels/) for larger projects.

faqs.q: What is Dibond?
faqs.a: Dibond is a well-known brand of aluminium composite material (ACM): two aluminium sheets with a polyethylene core. 'Dibond sign' is commonly used for any aluminium composite sign.

faqs.q: How long do aluminium signs last outside?
faqs.a: Printed and laminated aluminium composite signs typically last many years outdoors. Lifespan depends on exposure, so tell us if your sign faces full sun or the coast.

faqs.q: Can you print on brushed aluminium?
faqs.a: Yes. We print on brushed silver and brushed brass-effect panels, leaving the brushed metal showing through wherever there's no ink.

faqs.q: Can aluminium signs be cut to shape?
faqs.a: Yes. We can cut panels to the outline of your logo or any custom shape. Send a vector file with the cut path.

intro: Foamex signs are light, rigid and great value. Foamex is a brand name for foam PVC board: a smooth, solid plastic sheet with a lightweight core. It prints well, cuts cleanly and is easy to fix, which makes it a favourite for shop signs, menus, exhibitions, office signs and short-term outdoor use.
We print foamex boards in full colour, most commonly on 5mm white board. Black and recycled boards are also available, and any board can be cut to the outline of your logo or a custom shape.

Indoors, foamex lasts for years. Outdoors it's best for short to medium-term signs, such as promotions, events and temporary site signs, because strong sun and temperature changes can make it bow over time. For permanent outdoor signs we'd usually suggest [Dibond aluminium](/business-signs/dibond-aluminium-signs/).
Compare materials in our [foamex vs aluminium composite vs correx guide](/signage-home/compare/foamex-vs-aluminium-composite-vs-correx/).

faqs.q: Is foamex waterproof?
faqs.a: Yes, foam PVC doesn't absorb water. It's the long-term effect of sun and heat outdoors that limits its lifespan, not rain.

faqs.q: How long does foamex last outdoors?
faqs.a: Usually a year or two in an exposed spot, often longer in shade. Indoors it lasts for many years.

faqs.q: Foamex or Dibond?
faqs.a: Foamex is lighter and cheaper, ideal indoors and for temporary outdoor signs. Dibond (aluminium composite) is the better choice for permanent outdoor signs.

faqs.q: What thickness is foamex?
faqs.a: Our printed foamex signs are 5mm, which is rigid enough for most wall and display signs.

intro: Correx signs are the quick, low-cost answer for temporary signage. Correx is fluted polypropylene board, the twin-wall plastic you see on estate agent boards, building sites and event signs. It's waterproof, very light and tough enough to survive being moved around.
We print correx in full colour, in sizes up to 2440mm x 1220mm. Boards can be cable-tied to railings and Heras fencing, fixed to posts or stakes, or simply screwed to a fence.

Use correx for site signs, directional signs for events, open days and car boot sales, political and campaign signs, and short-term promotions. For signs that need to last years, choose [Dibond aluminium](/business-signs/dibond-aluminium-signs/) instead.

See how correx compares in our [foamex vs aluminium composite vs correx guide](/signage-home/compare/foamex-vs-aluminium-composite-vs-correx/), or browse [construction site signs](/business-signs/hoarding-boards/).

faqs.q: How long do correx signs last?
faqs.a: Typically six months to a year outdoors, depending on exposure. They're made for temporary use.

faqs.q: Can correx signs go on posts?
faqs.a: Yes. Correx can be fixed to wooden or metal posts with screws or cable ties, or slotted onto stakes.

faqs.q: Correx or foamex?
faqs.a: Correx is lighter, cheaper and better for rough outdoor use. Foamex has a smoother, more premium finish and is better for indoor display.

faqs.q: Is correx waterproof?
faqs.a: Yes, correx is polypropylene and won't absorb water.

intro: 3D letters turn your name or logo into something people notice. Built-up lettering stands proud of the wall and catches the light, so even a simple name looks considered and premium. They're popular for receptions, shopfronts, showrooms and office walls.

Choose from acrylic, metal and foamex letters. Acrylic letters come in gloss or matt black and white, or painted to any RAL colour to match your brand. Metal letters are available in brushed aluminium, stainless steel and gold finishes. Foamex and polystyrene letters are light and economical for large-scale or temporary displays.

Letters are cut from your artwork, so your font and logo stay exactly as designed. Fix them flat with strong tape, or on hidden stand-offs for a floating shadow effect. We supply a paper template so each letter goes in the right place.

For a sign that works after dark, see our [illuminated letters](/business-signs/illuminated-signs/). Comparing styles? Read [built-up letters vs flat panel signs](/signage-home/compare/built-up-letters-vs-flat-panel-signs/), or see our [built-up 3D letters service](/signage-home/building-signage-shop-signs/built-up-3d-letters/) for fitted shopfront lettering.

faqs.q: How are 3D letters fitted?
faqs.a: Either with VHB tape on smooth walls or with hidden stand-offs drilled into the wall. We supply a template showing exactly where each letter goes.

faqs.q: Can you match my brand colours?
faqs.a: Yes. Painted acrylic letters can be matched to a RAL colour, and printed options can match your brand colours closely.

faqs.q: Can 3D letters go outside?
faqs.a: Many can, including metal and acrylic letters. Check the product page, or ask us about your location.

faqs.q: Can you make my logo in 3D, not just text?
faqs.a: Yes. Send your logo as a vector file and we'll cut it as one piece or in layers.

intro: Illuminated signs keep your business visible after dark and make a strong statement during the day. Modern LED lighting is bright, efficient and long-lasting, so a lit sign costs far less to run than older fluorescent tube signs.

There are a few styles to choose from. Face-lit letters glow through their fronts for maximum visibility from the street. Halo-lit signs shine onto the wall behind for a soft, premium glow. Edge-lit acrylic lights up through the edges of the panel, and colour-changing LED letters let you switch colours with a remote. For shop fascias, an illuminated tray sign lights your whole name panel.

Every illuminated sign needs a power supply, and most need fitting by a competent installer. We can fit across Norfolk and Suffolk, including the electrical connection. If you're further away, ask your electrician to review the installation details before ordering.

Illuminated signs usually need advertisement consent from your local council, and rules are stricter in conservation areas. Our [planning consent for shop signs guide](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/planning-consent-for-shop-signs/) explains the basics, and [illuminated vs non-illuminated shop signs](/signage-home/compare/illuminated-vs-non-illuminated-shop-signs/) helps you decide. See also our [lightbox signs](/business-signs/lightbox-signs/).

faqs.q: Do illuminated signs need planning permission?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Most illuminated signs need advertisement consent from your local planning authority. Check with your council before ordering, especially in a conservation area or on a listed building.

faqs.q: How much does an LED sign cost to run?
faqs.a: LED signs use very little electricity, typically a few pence per hour for a typical shop sign. Your exact cost depends on the sign size and how long it's lit.

faqs.q: Halo-lit or face-lit?
faqs.a: Face-lit letters are brighter and easier to read from a distance. Halo-lit signs give a softer, more upmarket effect. Many shopfronts use face-lit; receptions often choose halo-lit.

faqs.q: Can you install it?
faqs.a: Yes, we install illuminated signs for businesses in Norfolk and Suffolk. Elsewhere, a qualified electrician should make the connection.

intro: Lightbox signs are bright, simple and very effective. A lightbox is a slim case with LEDs inside and a printed face on the front, so your logo and message glow evenly day and night.

Projecting light boxes stick out from the building at right angles, so people walking along the pavement can see you from both directions. They're a high-street favourite for cafés, takeaways, pharmacies, barbers and bars. We make them in round, square and rectangular shapes, with metal or aluminium bodies and printed faces on both sides.
For a warmer look inside, our wooden light box is ideal for cafés, boutiques and reception desks. The printed face can be replaced later if your branding changes, without replacing the whole sign.

Projecting signs normally need advertisement consent. Read our [planning consent for shop signs guide](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/planning-consent-for-shop-signs/) and see our fitted [projecting signs service](/signage-home/building-signage-shop-signs/projecting-signs/). Browse more [illuminated signs](/business-signs/illuminated-signs/) or non-lit [hanging signs](/business-signs/hanging-signs/).

faqs.q: Do projecting signs need permission?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Illuminated and projecting signs generally need advertisement consent from the council, and building owner approval if you rent.

faqs.q: Can the graphics be changed later?
faqs.a: Yes. The printed faces can be replaced if your branding or message changes.

faqs.q: Are lightboxes double-sided?
faqs.a: Our projecting light boxes are double-sided, so they can be seen from both directions along the street.

faqs.q: How are projecting light boxes fixed?
faqs.a: With a wall bracket fixed securely into the building. They need a power supply, and we recommend professional installation.

intro: Hanging signs are the traditional way to catch the eye of people walking along the street. Mounted on a bracket at right angles to the building, they're visible from both directions, which a flat fascia sign can't manage. Pubs, cafés, boutiques, galleries and high-street shops all use them.

We make hanging and projecting signs in metal, slate, foam PVC and printed panels, in square, round, rectangular and logo shapes. Most are printed on both sides. Brackets are available, or we can make signs to fit an existing bracket if you send us its measurements.

If your premises is in a conservation area or is a listed building, there may be rules on the size, material and style of hanging signs. Natural finishes such as slate and painted metal are often well received. Our [planning consent for shop signs guide](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/planning-consent-for-shop-signs/) has more detail.

Want it lit? See our [illuminated hanging sign](/business-signs/hanging-signs/illuminated-hanging-sign/) and [projecting light boxes](/business-signs/lightbox-signs/), or our fitted [projecting signs service](/signage-home/building-signage-shop-signs/projecting-signs/).

faqs.q: Do I need permission for a hanging sign?
faqs.a: Non-illuminated hanging signs often have deemed consent within limits, but rules vary, and conservation areas and listed buildings are stricter. Check with your local council.

faqs.q: What bracket do I need?
faqs.a: The bracket should suit the sign's size and weight. We supply brackets for our hanging signs and can advise if you're reusing an old one.

faqs.q: Can you match an existing bracket?
faqs.a: Yes. Send us the bracket's measurements, and the hanging hole spacing, and we'll size the sign to fit.

faqs.q: Are hanging signs double-sided?
faqs.a: Most are printed on both sides so the sign reads from either direction.

intro: Pavement signs and A-boards are one of the cheapest ways to bring passing trade through your door. Put your offer, menu or opening hours right where people walk, and change the message whenever you like.

Choose the style that suits your business. Printed A-boards carry your branding in full colour. Chalkboard A-boards let you write daily specials. Poster and snap-frame A-boards let you swap printed posters in seconds. Swinging and spring-based pavement signs move with the wind instead of blowing over, which makes them ideal for exposed forecourts.

Wooden A-boards in natural, painted and whitewashed finishes suit cafés, pubs and independent shops, while steel and plastic frames are tough and practical. We also make tabletop chalkboards and framed wall chalkboards for inside.

Placing an A-board on the public pavement may need permission or a licence from your council, and it must leave room for pedestrians, wheelchairs and pushchairs. Check the rules where you trade. For seating areas, see our [cafe barriers](/business-signs/cafe-barriers/).

faqs.q: Do I need a licence for an A-board?
faqs.a: Often, yes, if it stands on the public highway. Rules vary by council, so check with yours. Signs on your own forecourt usually don't need a licence.

faqs.q: Which A-board copes best with wind?
faqs.a: Swinging pavement signs on spring or water-filled bases cope best, because the panel moves with gusts instead of catching them.

faqs.q: Can I change the posters or graphics?
faqs.a: Yes. Poster and snap-frame A-boards take standard poster sizes, and printed panels can be reprinted.

faqs.q: What size A-board should I choose?
faqs.a: A1 (around 600 x 840mm) is the most popular. A0 and giant signs suit forecourts and roadsides; A2 suits narrow pavements and indoor use.

intro: Cafe barriers mark out your outdoor seating area and advertise your business at the same time. Printed banners stretch between upright posts on weighted bases, creating a smart, defined space for tables and chairs.

Choose a black or polished chrome frame, and order banners printed on one side or both. Extension kits let you add more length as your seating grows, and banners can be reprinted when your branding or menu changes.

Barriers are free-standing, so there's no drilling into the pavement, and they come apart for storage at the end of the day. If your seating is on the public highway you'll usually need a pavement licence from your council, which may set out where barriers can go.
Pair barriers with [pavement signs](/business-signs/pavement-signs/) and [hanging signs](/business-signs/hanging-signs/) for a complete outdoor look.

faqs.q: Do I need permission for cafe barriers?
faqs.a: If they're on the public pavement, your council will usually require a pavement licence. Barriers on private land don't normally need permission.

faqs.q: Can I replace just the banners?
faqs.a: Yes. Banners are replaceable, so you can update the design without buying new frames.

faqs.q: Are cafe barriers stable in the wind?
faqs.a: Weighted bases keep them steady in normal conditions. In strong winds, bring them in or remove the banners.

intro: Parking signs keep car parks organised and make it clear who can park where. Whether you're reserving bays for staff and visitors, marking disabled spaces or setting out rules for a private car park, clear signs prevent arguments and keep traffic moving safely.

Our car park signs cover visitor, staff, customer, permit, residents and disabled parking, as well as speed limits, reverse parking, directional arrows and private road and property notices. Most are available in several sizes, in portrait or landscape, and many come with arrow options.

Signs are made from weatherproof materials for outdoor use and can be fixed to walls, fences or posts. If you need different wording, your logo, or a whole set of matching signs for a site, we can make custom parking signs to order.

Looking for signs to stop people parking? See [no parking signs](/business-signs/parking-signs/no-parking-signs/). For more safety signage, browse our [safety and warning signs](/signage-home/site-safety-signs/safety-and-warning-signs/).

faqs.q: Are private parking signs enforceable?
faqs.a: Signs show your rules, but enforcing parking charges on private land must follow the relevant parking code of practice, with signs that meet its requirements. If you plan to enforce, speak to an approved parking operator first.

faqs.q: Can you add our logo or custom wording?
faqs.a: Yes. We can make any parking sign with your own wording, colours and logo.

faqs.q: Which material lasts best outdoors?
faqs.a: Aluminium composite is the most durable choice for permanent outdoor parking signs.

faqs.q: Can parking signs go on posts?
faqs.a: Yes. They can be fixed to posts, walls, fences and railings. See our [post mounted signs](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/).

intro: No parking signs protect your access: driveways, gates, entrances, garages and loading bays. A clear, polite sign is often all it takes to stop people blocking you in.

Choose from standard no parking signs and specific messages such as 'Do not block driveway', 'No parking in front of these gates', 'Access required 24 hours' and 'Keep entrance clear'. Many come with a 'Polite notice' header option, which tends to get a better response from neighbours and visitors.
Signs are weatherproof, in sizes from A4 up to 80cm wide, and can be fixed to walls, gates, fences or posts. Need different wording? We can make custom no parking signs too.

A sign on private property shows your wishes, but it doesn't make obstructing a driveway a criminal offence on its own. For managed car parks and enforcement, see our [parking signs](/business-signs/parking-signs/).

faqs.q: Can I put a no parking sign on my driveway?
faqs.a: Yes, you can put a sign on your own property. It makes your wishes clear, although it doesn't give you powers to fine or remove vehicles.

faqs.q: Which size is easiest to read?
faqs.a: For gates and driveways seen from the road, 40 x 30cm or larger works well. Use A4 (29.7 x 21cm) for doors and close-up positions.

faqs.q: Can you print custom wording?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us what you need it to say and we'll make it to order.

faqs.q: What does 'polite notice' mean on a sign?
faqs.a: It's a header that softens the message. Many people find it gets a better response than a blunt 'No parking'.

intro: PVC banners and other printed banners are the most cost-effective way to get a big message in front of a lot of people. They're quick to produce, easy to put up and reusable, which makes them perfect for shopfronts, events, building sites, sports clubs and schools.

PVC banners are the all-rounder: tough, waterproof and printed in full colour, with hemmed edges and eyelets for fixing. Mesh banners are perforated so wind passes through, which makes them safer and longer-lasting on fences, scaffolding and exposed sites. Heras fence banners are sized to fit standard temporary fencing panels.
Our banner range also includes feather flags, lamp post banners and frames. Freestanding and wall-mounted frames hold banners taut and make them easy to swap.

Unsure which material to choose? Read [PVC vs mesh banners](/signage-home/compare/pvc-vs-mesh-banners/) or see our [mesh banners service](/signage-home/large-format-print/mesh-banners/). For indoor events, see [roller banners](/business-signs/roller-banners/).

faqs.q: PVC or mesh banner?
faqs.a: PVC is best on walls and in sheltered spots, and has a more solid look. Mesh is better on fences, railings and scaffolding, where wind would catch a solid banner.

faqs.q: How long do outdoor banners last?
faqs.a: A well-fixed PVC or mesh banner can last for several years outdoors, depending on exposure and how it's tensioned.

faqs.q: How do I fix a banner to railings?
faqs.a: Use cable ties or bungee ties through the eyelets, spaced evenly so the banner stays taut.

faqs.q: What size banner do I need?
faqs.a: Think about reading distance: a banner seen from a road needs large text. We can advise on size and layout.

intro: Roller banners are the easiest display you'll ever put up. The printed graphic rolls down into a base, then pulls up and clips onto a pole in under a minute. Also called pull up banners or roll up banners, they're ideal for exhibitions, receptions, events and in-store promotions.

Choose a standard stand for great value, or a premium stand for a sturdier base and a smoother mechanism that lasts through regular use. Widths run from 800mm to 2000mm, and every banner comes with a carry bag.
For outdoor events, our outdoor roller banner has a weighted, wind-resistant base and can take a PVC or mesh graphic.

Still choosing? Our [budget vs premium pull-up banners comparison](/signage-home/compare/budget-vs-premium-pull-up-banners/) explains the difference, or see our [pull-up banners service](/signage-home/signage-exhibition-stands/pull-up-banners/). For bigger displays, browse [pop up stands](/business-signs/exhibition-displays/).

faqs.q: Budget or premium roller banner?
faqs.a: Standard stands are perfect for occasional use. Choose premium if you'll use it often, travel with it, or want a sturdier base.

faqs.q: Can I replace the graphic?
faqs.a: Yes, on premium stands the graphic can be replaced, so you can update your banner without a new stand.

faqs.q: What size roller banner should I choose?
faqs.a: 850mm wide is the most popular. Wider banners make a bigger backdrop for events and photo walls.

faqs.q: Can roller banners be used outside?
faqs.a: Standard indoor banners aren't made for wind. Use our outdoor roller banner for outside events.

intro: Pop up stands and exhibition displays give your stand real presence without a custom build. They're portable, quick to set up and reusable from show to show.

Pop up displays use a folding frame with printed panels, in straight or curved shapes and widths from around 1.2m to over 4m. Fabric display stands use a lightweight frame with a stretched, printed fabric graphic for a seamless, crease-free look. Fabric backdrops work well for photo walls, presentations and events.
For permanent spaces, wall-mounted fabric frames turn printed fabric into smart, changeable wall graphics for receptions and showrooms.

Planning a show? See our [exhibition stand checklist](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/exhibition-stand-checklist/) and our [pop-up displays service](/signage-home/signage-exhibition-stands/pop-up-displays/). Add [roller banners](/business-signs/roller-banners/) to complete your stand.

faqs.q: How long does a pop up stand take to set up?
faqs.a: Usually 10 to 20 minutes for one person, once you've done it once.

faqs.q: Fabric or PVC graphics?
faqs.a: Fabric is lighter, folds without creasing and looks seamless. PVC panels are more rigid and wipe clean easily.

faqs.q: Can I reuse the frame with new graphics?
faqs.a: Yes. Frames are reusable, so you can order new graphics for future events.

intro: Outdoor signs for business need to be clear from a distance and tough enough to last. Whether it's a sign at your site entrance, a totem by the road or directional signs around a business park, the right material and mounting make all the difference.

Post-mounted signs put your panel on one or two posts at the height you need, with post lengths, colours and bases to suit the ground. Freestanding totem and monolith signs make a bold statement at entrances, car parks and forecourts. Spike signs push into grass for temporary use, and printed bollard covers turn plain bollards into advertising.
Panels are made from durable, weatherproof materials such as aluminium composite. Larger freestanding signs need secure foundations, and may need planning consent, so speak to us about installation.

Read [how long outdoor signs last](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/how-long-do-outdoor-signs-last/), or browse [Dibond aluminium signs](/business-signs/dibond-aluminium-signs/) and [parking signs](/business-signs/parking-signs/).

faqs.q: Do freestanding signs need planning permission?
faqs.a: Larger freestanding signs and totems often need advertisement consent. Check with your council, especially if the sign is lit or near a road.

faqs.q: How are post signs installed?
faqs.a: Posts are usually concreted into the ground, or bolted to a base plate on hard surfaces. We can install signs in Norfolk and Suffolk.

faqs.q: How long do outdoor signs last?
faqs.a: Aluminium composite signs with a protective laminate typically last many years. Location and sun exposure make a difference.

We print full-colour hoarding panels with an anti-graffiti protective layer, so tags and marker pen can be cleaned off. Panels are sized to suit standard hoarding runs and can show site plans, computer-generated images of the finished development, contact details and safety messages.

For temporary fencing, add [Heras fence banners](/business-signs/banners/heras-fence-banner/) or [correx site signs](/business-signs/correx-signs/). For safety signage, see our [safety and warning signs](/signage-home/site-safety-signs/safety-and-warning-signs/).

faqs.q: How are hoarding boards fixed?

faqs.q: Can graphics be replaced in sections?
faqs.a: Yes. Panels are printed individually, so damaged sections can be replaced without reprinting the whole run.

faqs.q: Do you add an anti-graffiti finish?
faqs.a: Yes, our printed hoarding boards come with an anti-graffiti protective layer.

intro: Reception signs are often the first thing a visitor sees, and they set the tone for everything that follows. A well-made logo on the reception wall tells people they're in the right place and that you take your brand seriously.

Choose a floating logo panel that stands off the wall for depth, a laser-cut name sign cut as a single piece, or a curved aluminium sign that sweeps out from the wall. For something bolder, add [3D letters](/business-signs/3d-letters/) or a [halo-lit logo](/business-signs/illuminated-signs/halo-lit-logo-sign/).
Think about size and viewing distance: your logo should read clearly from the entrance. Send us a photo of the wall and its measurements, and we'll suggest a size and show you a mock-up.

faqs.q: What size should a reception logo be?
faqs.a: It depends on the wall and viewing distance. As a rough guide, the logo should fill a third to a half of the wall's width. We can mock it up on a photo of your wall.

faqs.q: Can a reception sign be lit?

faqs.q: How is it installed?

intro: Wayfinding signs help people find their way around your building or site without having to ask. Good wayfinding reduces stress for visitors, saves staff time and helps everyone find exits and facilities quickly.

A wayfinding scheme usually combines directional signs with arrows, identification signs on doors and rooms, and floor or level signs. Our acrylic wayfinding signs come in portrait and landscape layouts with arrows in any direction, and our tactile braille signs make room and facility signs accessible to blind and partially sighted visitors.

Keep signs consistent in style, mount them at a sensible height, and make sure text contrasts strongly with the background. We can help plan a complete scheme for offices, schools, healthcare and public buildings.
See also [office signs](/business-signs/office-signs/) and [floor graphics](/business-signs/floor-graphics/) for wayfinding underfoot.

faqs.q: What height should signs be mounted?
faqs.a: Wall signs are commonly placed so the text sits roughly at eye level, around 1400 to 1700mm from the floor. Tactile signs need to be within easy reach.

faqs.q: Do we need braille signs?
faqs.a: Tactile and braille signs make buildings more accessible and are recommended for public buildings and workplaces. Accessibility guidance such as BS 8300 sets out good practice.

faqs.q: Can you plan a full scheme?
faqs.a: Yes. We can work from floor plans or visit your site to plan directional and door signs.

Repositionable fabric graphics and PVC-free materials suit rented spaces and greener fit-outs. Whiteboard and chalkboard wall vinyls turn any wall into a writing surface.

faqs.q: Do you measure and fit?

faqs.q: Can wall graphics be removed?

intro: Window graphics make the most of your glass. Use them to advertise your business, add privacy, meet glass safety requirements or simply make your premises look more professional.

Frosted window film gives a sandblasted-glass look that lets light through while blocking the view, ideal for offices, clinics and meeting rooms. Printed frosted film adds your logo or a pattern. One way vision lets you see out while the outside shows a full-colour print, and blockout graphics hide what's behind completely. Shop window stickers can be cut to any shape for offers and branding.

Large areas of glass in doors and screens may need manifestation, markings that make the glass visible, so people don't walk into it. Our [glass manifestation regulations guide](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/glass-manifestation-regulations/) explains the requirements.

We can measure and fit window graphics in Norfolk and Suffolk. See our [frosted manifestation](/signage-home/window-graphics/frosted-manifestation/) and [privacy film](/signage-home/window-graphics/privacy-film/) services.

faqs.q: Do glass doors need manifestation?
faqs.a: Large glazed doors and screens in workplaces generally need markings to make the glass visible. Our manifestation guide covers the requirements.

faqs.q: Can you see out through one way vision?
faqs.a: Yes. From inside you can see out through the perforations; from outside people see the printed graphic.

faqs.q: Do window graphics go inside or outside the glass?
faqs.a: Most go on the inside, which protects them from the weather. Some printed graphics are applied outside for the best colour.

faqs.q: Can window film be removed?
faqs.a: Yes. Vinyl window graphics peel off and any residue cleans off the glass.

intro: Floor graphics put your message where people are looking: down. They're great for wayfinding, promotions, queue management and event branding, in shops, warehouses, venues and outdoor spaces.

Our printed floor stickers are laminated with an anti-slip, R11-rated finish for safety indoors. Outdoor floor graphics are made for pavements and concrete, and multi-surface vinyl grips brick, block paving and textured walls. For events and showrooms, printed carpet and printed lino give full-colour floors.
Floors should be clean and dry before application. Most floor graphics are designed for short to medium-term use and peel off cleanly when you're finished.
See also [wall graphics](/business-signs/wall-graphics/) and [logo mats](/business-signs/logo-mats/).

faqs.q: Are floor graphics slippery?
faqs.a: Our floor graphics are laminated with an anti-slip finish rated R11, or R12 for the multi-surface vinyl.

faqs.q: How long do floor graphics last?
faqs.a: It depends on foot traffic. In busy areas, expect several months; in quieter spots, longer.

faqs.q: Can floor graphics go outside?
faqs.a: Yes, our outdoor floor graphics and multi-surface vinyl are made for external surfaces.

intro: Wooden business signs and slate signs bring warmth and character that plastic and metal can't match. They suit cafés, farm shops, holiday lets, pubs, garden centres and any business with a natural or rustic feel, and look just as good in modern offices.

We print and engrave plywood and MDF signs, cut wooden signs to the shape of your logo, and pair timber with brushed aluminium for a contemporary look. Slate signs come with natural riven edges or a smooth honed finish, printed with your logo or combined with clear acrylic.
Wood used outside benefits from a weather-resistant coating, and slate is naturally durable. Indoors, both last for years with very little care.
Browse our [hanging signs](/business-signs/hanging-signs/), including slate hanging signs, or see [pavement signs](/business-signs/pavement-signs/) in wooden finishes.

faqs.q: Can wooden signs go outside?
faqs.a: Yes, with a weather-resistant coating. Plywood is more suitable than MDF for outdoor use.

faqs.q: Engraved or printed?
faqs.a: Engraving cuts into the wood for a natural, tactile finish. Printing allows full colour and fine detail.

faqs.q: How do I care for a slate sign?
faqs.a: Wipe it with a damp cloth. Slate is naturally weatherproof and needs very little care.

description: Post mounted signs put your message at exactly the right height, wherever there's no wall to fix to. This double post sign holds a panel up to 2000 x 1000mm between two sturdy posts, making it ideal for site entrances, car parks, business estates, farms, schools and roadside positions.

Choose your post height (1.5, 2 or 2.5 metres), post diameter (50mm or 76mm for larger signs), post colour (silver, black, grey or white) and whether you need base plates for fixing to hard surfaces.

faqs.q: Can the panel be replaced later?
faqs.a: Yes, the panel can be swapped without replacing the posts.

description: A curved totem sign is one of the most effective ways to announce your business at a site entrance. Standing up to three metres tall, it's seen from the road, from the car park and from across a business estate, long before anyone reaches your door. The gently curved faces catch the light and give the sign a modern, architectural shape that a flat board can't match.

Each totem is built around a welded aluminium tray, powder coated in the RAL colour of your choice, with a steel framework inside for strength. Your graphics are digitally printed, laminated for protection and applied to the front, or to both front and back so the sign works for traffic coming from either direction. The result is a solid, freestanding monolith that looks at home outside offices, retail parks, schools, hotels, care homes and industrial units.

Choose from four standard sizes: 1000 or 1500mm wide, and 2000 or 3000mm tall. If those don't suit your site, we can make the totem to a bespoke size, add 3D lettering or logos to the faces, or build in illumination so it stays visible after dark.

A totem is a long-term investment in your site's first impression, so it's worth planning it properly. Think about where drivers will first see it, how far away they'll be when they need to read it, and what they need to know: your name, a logo, perhaps the businesses on a shared site and a phone number or web address. Keep it simple and it will work hard for years.

Comparing styles? The [flat totem sign](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/totem-sign/) has the same construction with flat faces. Browse all [outdoor signs](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/) or read [how long outdoor signs last](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/how-long-do-outdoor-signs-last/).

install: Totems are installed by setting the steel posts into concrete footings. The posts extend roughly 600mm below the finished ground level, so the footings need to be dug deeper than that. The ground conditions, any underground services and the sign's exposure to wind all affect the footing size, so we recommend professional installation.

We install totems across Norfolk and Suffolk. Elsewhere, we can supply the totem ready for your groundworker or contractor to install. Freestanding signs of this size often need advertisement consent, especially near roads or if illuminated, so check with your council before ordering; our [planning consent guide](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/planning-consent-for-shop-signs/) explains the basics.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a curved and a flat totem?
faqs.a: Both have the same construction. On a curved totem the front and back faces have a gentle curve; on a [flat totem](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/totem-sign/) they're completely flat. Curved faces look more contemporary and catch the light; flat faces give a crisper, more traditional look.

faqs.q: How is a totem sign installed?
faqs.a: The steel posts are concreted into footings deeper than about 600mm. We install in Norfolk and Suffolk, or your contractor can install it using our guidance.

faqs.q: Are the graphics on both sides?
faqs.a: You can choose single or double-sided graphics. Double-sided is best if the totem will be seen by traffic coming from both directions. Graphics go on the front faces, not the narrow sides.

faqs.q: Can I have a different size or add lighting?
faqs.a: Yes. We can make bespoke sizes, add 3D lettering or logos, and build in illumination. Tell us what you need and we'll quote.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a totem sign?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Large freestanding signs and illuminated signs usually need advertisement consent. Check with your local planning authority before ordering.

faqs.q: Can the graphics be updated later?
faqs.a: Yes. The printed vinyl graphics can be replaced, for example if a tenant on a shared site changes, without replacing the totem.

uses: Shared sites: list multiple tenants on one sign
install: The totem's steel posts are set into concrete footings deeper than about 600mm. We install in Norfolk and Suffolk, or can supply the sign for your contractor.
Large freestanding signs often need advertisement consent; check with your council first. See our [planning consent guide](/signage-home/guides-and-advice/planning-consent-for-shop-signs/).

faqs.q: Flat or curved totem?
faqs.a: They're built the same way. Flat faces give a crisp, classic look; [curved faces](/business-signs/outdoor-signs/curved-totem-sign/) look more contemporary.

faqs.q: Can you list several businesses on one totem?
faqs.a: Yes. Totems are ideal for shared sites, and individual name panels can be replaced as tenants change.

faqs.q: How tall should my totem be?
faqs.a: Two metres suits most car park and entrance positions; three metres gives more visibility from roads and across large sites.

faqs.q: Do totems need planning permission?
faqs.a: Often, yes, especially near roads or if illuminated. Check with your local planning authority.

faqs.q: Can it be illuminated?
faqs.a: Yes, we can build in lighting. Ask us for a quote.
